chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The merchant delays himself regarding Hajj.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no excuse for him, and if he were to die, he would have left a law from the laws of Islam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a merchant delays Hajj due to trade?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for a merchant, the demands of trade do not constitute a valid excuse (‘udhr) for postponing Hajj once the conditions of ability (istita’ah) are met. The severity of this neglect is highlighted by the statement that dying in this state equates to abandoning a fundamental pillar of Islam, emphasizing the urgency of fulfilling this obligation without unnecessary delay.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd Al Shahaam who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The business man delays himself for the Hajj’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no excuse for him, and if he were to die, so he would have neglected a Law from the Laws of Al-Islam’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
There is a merchant who procrastinates in performing al-Hajj. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he does it without good reason, he has violated one of the laws of al-Islam.’”
